    Socle ideals of primitive projective-injective right modules #

    Let eA be one member of a complete duplicate-free family of primitive projective right ideals. If eA is injective, then its socle, embedded in the regular right module, is stable under left multiplication and hence is a two-sided ideal. This is the algebraic first step of the rejection lemma.

    The proof is the Auslander--Reiten argument in coordinates. A nonzero off-diagonal component eA → fA on the simple essential socle would be monic; injectivity of eA would split it; and indecomposability of fA would then make the two selected primitive projectives isomorphic, contradicting the duplicate-free skeleton.
